text.p: Surinam Public Works Minister Richard Kalloe has resigned and political sources said his departure was caused by divisions within the new coalition government of President Jules Wijdenbosch.
Kalloe, a prominent member of the newly-formed Liberation Party for Freedom and Democracy (BVD), told a news conference late on Monday he was taking up a job in the private sector.

But political sources said his resignation was prompted by differences between the business-oriented BVD and the National Democratic Party (NDP) of Wijdenbosch and former military strongman Desi Bouterse.
They said the BVD, one of five parties in the government, wants the new administration to speed up the economic modernisation of the small former Dutch colony, including a series of privatisations.
Wijdenbosch, who took office in September after winning a narrow presidential runoff against former President Ronald Venetiaan, is said to be against large-scale privatisation.

A multi-racial country of 400,000 and one of the world's biggest bauxite producers, Surinam is slowly emerging from an economic recession that has seen gross domestic product per capita cut from $3,000 to $1,200 in the last 15 years.
No replacement for Kalloe was immediately named.
